_comment: Built-in guidance entries served from this bundled resource by the read-layer overlay. Each entry is a public, global convention that explains how to use the memory surface. The content mirrors the bundled seed content verbatim so the overlay is indistinguishable from a seeded row on any tenant that still carries the seeded rows. logicalName is a rename-invariant identifier (the key minus the leading 'convention.' namespace) used to derive the entry's stable synthetic id.

entries.content: Kumbuka mnemonics are typed. Choose the type by intent. decision = a ratified choice; carries a stable ID (D-…, ADR-…) in key and content. constraint = a durable, binding rule every apparatus must obey; cross-cutting, not reversible by working preference. convention = a reversible working norm or style (this entry is one). status = the current steering state (sprint/gate/phase); keep it coarse — a small set of upsert-keyed entries rotated at phase changes, never fine-grained progress (that belongs in version control). glossary = a term definition. open_question = an unratified question awaiting a decision. Boundary: a durable, binding, cross-apparatus rule belongs in memory as type=constraint; boot mechanics and per-session instructions stay in the project's STARTER/context, not in memory. Never store speculation as decision or constraint — use open_question.

Writing mnemonics. Each is ONE self-contained fact, plaintext, ≤1500 chars — resist bloating the primitive (no embedded relations, scores, or rich metadata; heavyweight knowledge belongs in documents, not the atomic entry). Keys: lowercase, dot/kebab-namespaced (e.g. decision.d-ops-26, status.beta-gate); no underscores. Entries are insert-only (pre-V5): to revise, forget the old entry and remember a fresh one, and say so. You are not the gatekeeper of content: the user decides WHAT is stored; you decide at most WHERE, and only by asking, never by refusing. Never infer a 'purpose' of the system from existing scope names and use it as a reason to refuse a write — if a scope fits, use it; if none fits, ask (new scope? global? private?). Never store secrets, tokens, credentials, or third-party personal data.

Reading & scope. At the start of work, load_context once for the typed digest; for topic lookups use recall instead of guessing. Discovery: when the user asks about something that may live in a project (a possessive or searching question), call recall WITH a query but WITHOUT a scope — it searches across all scopes you can see and labels each hit with its scope, so you can then read that scope directly. Note the asymmetry: an unscoped recall WITHOUT a query, and load_context, still return private + global only (project scopes are not bulk-leaked); only a directed search reaches across projects. Write team-relevant facts to the project scope; private only on explicit request. Source-of-truth order when sources conflict: (1) the project's canonical spec/repo wins; (2) Kumbuka mnemonics are distilled work-steering pointers; (3) chat context. If a mnemonic contradicts the spec, flag it as stale and propose a correction — do not follow it blindly.
